title: UniQure crashes as Huntington’s gene therapy shows less slowing of disease at 4 years
snippet: The results are nevertheless “unprecedented,” UniQure executives said on an investor call Tuesday, emphasizing that the updated natural history database used as the control group for the Phase 1/2 study of AMT-130 underestimates disease progression.

title: Roche cuts muscle-sparing obesity drug after mid-stage disappointment
snippet: Roche’s anti-myostatin therapy emugrobart is unlikely to elicit meaningful weight loss, according to an interim mid-stage analysis, prompting the pharma to return the asset rights to its subsidiary Chugai Pharmaceutical.

title: Summit snags $2B investment from AstraZeneca, clearing financial overhang
snippet: The all-stock deal gives Summit Therapeutics enough money to see through Phase 3 trials for the PD-1/VEGF bispecific ivonescimab—but keeps the asset fully in-house without giving up licensing rights.

title: Novo adds long-term obesity differentiation in up to $2.6B Hengrui deal
snippet: Investors looking for more transformative business development at Novo will have to wait, but a new partnership with China’s Hengrui Pharma adds a new weekly oral option to the Danish pharma’s early pipeline.

title: 3 steps for taking on Novartis in radiopharma: Curium up first
snippet: To successfully challenge Novartis on two planned fronts, Curium will need to overcome the unique challenges posed by radiopharmaceutical supply to get products to patients and win market share.

title: Kodiak Sciences’ stock soars 166% after 2 assets match Eylea in Phase 3 trial
snippet: Kodiak Sciences will head to regulators with one of the candidates, an anti-VEGF antibody called zenkuda, after the late-stage results.

title: FDA nod for Mirum’s Atebrioz makes 3 options for ultra-rare bone disease
snippet: The approval of Mirum Pharmaceuticals’ ALK2 inhibitor for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva on Friday adds a third option for patients who had long been without any treatments, joining Regeneron’s recently approved Pasatru and Ipsen’s Sohonos.

title: Merck inks up to $2.13B deal to dine with SciBrunch, gain rights to preclinical KRAS inhibitor
snippet: Merck continues to diversify its cancer efforts as the clock ticks down on Keytruda’s patent, picking up rights to a preclinical oncology asset in a deal that could exceed $2 billion.

title: Report: What Powers Employee Engagement
snippet: What drives meaningful employee engagement in today’s life sciences workplace? This BioSpace report explores the factors that shape how employees feel about their organizations and what employers can do to create workplaces where talent wants to stay and thrive.

title: AbbVie wins FDA approval for Parkinson’s drug from $8.7B Cerevel takeover
snippet: In the Phase 3 TEMPO program, AbbVie’s Juvmo elicited significant improvements in motor symptoms and prolonged periods with good symptom control.

title: Merck, Daiichi Sankyo retract accelerated approval request for lung cancer ADC
snippet: Merck and Daiichi Sankyo’s withdrawal of an accelerated approval request for the antibody-drug conjugate ifinatamab deruxtecan is a “net positive” for rivals like GSK and Roche, according to RBC Capital Markets.

title: Regenerative medicine needs more than stem cells
snippet: Stem cell therapies vary widely yet many physicians still treat them as interchangeable. A more credible model requires diagnostics, product characterization and conventional medical context to determine who and when should receive regenerative treatment.

title: Milestone Sanfilippo nod helps Ultragenyx regroup after tough Angelman defeat
snippet: The recent FDA approval of Fayuvi for a rare, childhood neurodegenerative disease was “particularly special” for Ultragenyx CEO Emil Kakkis. It could also, along with an August nod for another gene therapy, help offset recent challenges brought on by two asset failures.

title: 6 immunology targets to sustain a mammoth I&I market
snippet: Johnson & Johnson, Pfizer, Argenx and more are unlocking new immunology targets and looking to improve on existing ones in an attempt to catch some of the magic brought about by AbbVie’s Humira and Sanofi and Regeneron’s Dupixent.

title: After COVID, biomanufacturing tackles preparedness and commercialization challenges
snippet: Manufacturers are redesigning their processes to balance both better future emergency vaccine mobilization and the more demanding work of maintaining flexible, commercially viable manufacturing networks.

title: Nektar prevails in legal battle with Lilly over broken rezpeg partnership
snippet: Nektar Therapeutics has been awarded $90 million in damages after a jury sided with the biotech, which had accused Big Pharma Eli Lilly of “botching” an analysis of their formerly partnered autoimmune drug.

title: ADARx raises $446M in biotech’s third largest IPO of 2026, City files to go public
snippet: Two RNA biotechs, ADARx Pharmaceuticals and City Therapeutics, are taking advantage of the IPO frenzy, which has led to a total of 27 newly public biotechs so far this year.

title: J&J, Legend tout long-term survival benefits for Carvykti in multiple myeloma
snippet: Ten patients out of 20 who received Johnson & Johnson and Legend Biotech’s Carvykti remained alive at five years of follow up.

title: Genentech makes $1.5B+ deal with AI heavyweight Earendil for cancer bispecifics
snippet: Genentech's agreement with Earendil Labs came the same day its parent company, Roche, inked a cardiometabolic and renal deal with Atavistik Bio for up to $2 billion.

title: FDA slams GLP-1 compounder over risk of contaminating drugs ‘with filth’
snippet: FDA inspectors found evidence that the compounding pharmacy was making versions of Eli Lilly’s tirzepatide and Novo’s semaglutide “regularly or in inordinate amounts” at a site with “insanitary conditions.”

title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.

title: Biotech’s China problem: An issue of national security or economic value for the US?
snippet: Congressional letters sent to the CEOs of Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, BMS and AbbVie this week voicing concerns about the pharmas' clinical trials in China highlight an ongoing discrepancy in how government and industry think about the rise of the Asian country’s biotech industry.
